issues.title: Boundary majorization does not imply first-order tangency

failure_location.quote: Recall that $\nabla g_{n+1}^{(i)}(\theta_{n}^{(i)})=\nabla f_{n+1}^{(i)}(\theta_{n}^{(i)})$ since $g_{n}^{(i)}\ge f_{n}^{(i)}$ and $ g_{n+1}^{(i)}(\theta_{n}^{(i)})= f_{n+1}^{(i)}(\theta_{n}^{(i)})$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $h_{n}^{(i)}\ge 0$, $h_{n}^{(i)}(\theta_{n-1}^{(i)})=0$. Hence if we assume $h_{n}^{(i)}$ is differentiable, then necessarily $\nabla h_{n}^{(i)}(\theta_{n-1}^{(i)})=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 1 requires majorization only on the constrained domain and equal values, which do not imply equal gradients at a boundary. One-block Theta=[0,infinity), f(x)=(x-1)^2, x_0=0, g_n(x)=1+x+2x^2 yields h=3x+x^2>=x^2, exact x_n=0 forever, Delta_n=0, L_f=L_h=2, L_g=lambda=4, rho=2; all A1-A5 hold with r_n=infinity, but h_n'(0)=3. The key lemma is false: for b_n->0 its LHS is 2b_(n+1), while the RHS is L b_(n+1)^2/2. The stationary limit theorem is likewise false because S(0)=2.
issues.overall_effect: The first unsupported formal input occurs in the key complexity lemma. The same missing tangency premise directly defeats the gradient-gap bound and the asymptotic stationarity chain. Specific application surrogates that are demonstrably tangent are not automatically invalidated by this general-class omission.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add grad g_n^(i)(theta_(n-1)^(i))=grad f_n^(i)(theta_(n-1)^(i)) to sharpness. This is exactly the explicit v6 revision and legitimates the uses of tangency throughout the existing proof; standard BCD, proximal and prox-linear families are retained.
issues.why_classification: The repair restricts a natural class of allowed boundary-touching surrogates, so it exceeds an exceptional-degeneracy minor change, but it is contained and preserves comparable main guarantees. Moderate is the preferred projection.
issues.new_version_repair_locator: v5 unchanged; v6 line 390 explicitly adds gradient equality. v6 line 683 retains the old explanatory inference, but it is no longer needed once equality is assumed.

issues.title: Asymptotic exactness invokes surrogate strong convexity absent from its hypotheses
issues.failure_explanation: A3(b) lower-bounds the majorization gap h=g-f; it does not make g strongly convex. Let Theta=[-1,1], f(x)=(1-x^2)^2, g_n(x)=1, x_n=x_0=0, r_n=infinity, and choose the exact minimizer x_n*=1. Then h=2x^2-x^4>=x^2, tangency holds at 0, A1-A4 hold with rho=2 and Delta_n=0, but |x_n-x_n*|=1 for every n. Thus the proposition itself is false independently of the boundary-tangency issue.
issues.overall_effect: The standalone asymptotic-exactness result overstates its surrogate class. Later stationarity uses assume A5 or diminishing radii, where its intended conclusion is valid; they do not lose their guarantees from this root after the local hypothesis correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add A5(b), equivalently uniform strong convexity of g_n^(i), in the no-trust-region branch. Retain the existing radius argument in the diminishing-radius branch.
issues.why_classification: The literal supporting result loses a natural class of merely convex majorizers, so moderate is preferred under the policy that limited propagation does not lower root severity. Minor is a defensible alternative only if the local result is read under the section-wide A5 regime already required for every substantive use.
issues.new_version_repair_locator: v6 relocates this proposition and explicitly assumes strongly convex g at lines 839-840. Its proof retains stale case-split wording, but the missing premise is restored.

issues.title: NMF application assumes compact sublevels despite factor-scaling invariance

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\begin{customassumption}{A2} \label{assumption:A2}
		The objective function $f:\Param \rightarrow \R$ is continuously differentiable, and for each compact subset $\Param_{0}\subseteq \Param$, there exist a constant $L_{f}=L_{f}(\Param_{0})$ such that $\lVert \nabla f(x) - \nabla f(y) \rVert\le L_{f} \lVert x-y \rVert$ for all $x,y\in \Param_{0}$. Also, $f^{*}:=\inf_{\param\in \Param} f(\param)>-\infty$. Furthermore, the sub-level sets $f^{-1}((-\infty, a])=\{ \param\in \Param\,:\, f(\param)\le a \}$ for $a\in \R$ are compact.

Fix a matrix $X\in \R_{\ge 0}^{p \times N}$. Let $(\param_{n})_{n\ge 0}$, $\param_{n}:=(W_{n}, H_{n})$ be generated by \eqref{eq:MUPR_NMF} with arbitrary initialization $\param_{0}\in \Param:=\R_{\ge 0}^{p\times r}\times \R_{\ge 0}^{r\times N}$. Denote $f(W,H):=\frac{1}{2}\lVert X- WH \rVert_{F}^{2}$. Suppose the thresholding and proximal regularization parameters $\delta,\rho$ are strictly positive. Then the following hold:

A similar construction of surrogate function and claim will hold for $W_{n+1}$ by symmetry. Points \ref{NMF_claim_1}-\ref{NMF_claim_2} verify that \eqref{eq:MUPR_NMF} is a particular instance of BMM (Alg. \ref{algorithm:BMM-DR}). Given this, we can easily verify that the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{thm:complexity} holds for the NMF problem \eqref{eq:NMF} and the algorithm MUR \eqref{eq:MUPR_NMF}. Indeed, Assumptions \ref{assumption:A1} and \ref{assumption:A2} hold trivially. The restricted smoothness property of the majorization gap in \ref{assumption:A3} holds by point \ref{NMF_claim_4}. \ref{assumption:A3}\textbf{b} holds for $\rho>0$ due to point \ref{NMF_claim_3} (This is why we should require $\rho>0$ in Corollary \ref{cor:NMF}). \ref{assumption:A4} holds by point \ref{NMF_claim_2}. Lastly,  \ref{assumption:A5} holds by points \ref{NMF_claim_3} and \ref{NMF_claim_4}. This is enough to deduce Corollary \ref{cor:NMF} from Theorem \ref{thm:complexity}.

\item[(6)] A regularized version of the multiplicative update algorithm for nonnegative matrix/tensor factorization with guaranteed asymptotic convergence to stationary points and iteration complexity of $O(\eps^{-2} (\log \eps^{-1})^{2})$;

issues.failure_explanation: The proof invokes prop:boundedness without its compact-sublevel hypothesis A2. On the stated entire nonnegative factor space, f(tW,H/t)=f(W,H); even scalar X=1 has the unbounded zero-loss family (W,H)=(t,1/t). Thus the assertion that A1/A2 hold trivially is false, and neither bounded iterates nor a common L_h follows from that proposition.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed application of thm:complexity to cor:NMF is unsupported: compact sublevels do not hold, so the supplied argument provides neither bounded iterates nor the uniform smoothness needed along the trajectory. Consequently the advertised convergence and rate guarantees for MUR from arbitrary nonnegative initialisation are not established by this proof. This defect remains after granting the independent surrogate, update-order and complexity-quantifier corrections. It does not establish an actually divergent MUR trajectory.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: A supported repair retains only a bounded-run theorem: assume the generated trajectory is bounded and localise to a product of compact convex boxes containing all iterates and their original feasible unit neighbourhoods. Grant the independent update and theorem repairs. Each actual exact block minimiser remains a minimiser on the restricted domain, compact sublevels and uniform smoothness are available, and the original unit-ball stationarity residual agrees with the restricted residual along the run. This recovers original-domain stationarity and the fixed-run rate conditionally, but does not prove boundedness or unconditional coverage of arbitrary initialisations. A separate replacement-algorithm route normalises W columns to sum to one, absorbs their scales into H and minimises corrected touching surrogates over that normalised domain. Compactness and a stationarity-residual transfer support guarantees for this modified algorithm, whose W step is a weighted simplex projection. This route replaces the factor-domain and update contract of the advertised MUR method; it is not accepted here as a compatible repair preserving that method. Recovering the original unconditional MUR guarantee would require a separate valid boundedness argument or another compatible analysis, neither supplied by the compact-sublevel claim.
issues.why_classification: Serious: the supported bounded-run repair withdraws the unconditional convergence and rate guarantee for arbitrary permitted initialisations of the advertised MUR method, which is a central application claim in the abstract, contribution list and NMF corollary. This is major loss of an algorithmic guarantee, not merely a local premise correction. The normalised-factor construction proves a result for a redesigned algorithm with a simplex-constrained W update and is not treated as a compatible moderate repair of this MUR claim. The classification reflects the loss under the supported repair routes, not a claim that the iterates have been shown to diverge or that every possible future repair is impossible.
issues.new_version_repair_locator: premise_changed_but_full_repair_unverified: v6 adds compact initialisation/compact-factor discussion and replaces the boundedness proposition invocation with boundedness by hypothesis. Eq:MUPR_NMF still has no projection or normalisation. This is evidence of a change addressing the gap, not proof of a completed repair. v6 raw main.tex lines 1564, 1582-1583, 1674-1675. Exact version quotes are preserved in version-status.json, record APP-02.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $H_{n+1}$ in \eqref{eq:MUPR_NMF} is an exact minimizer of $g_{n}$ over $\R_{\ge 0}^{p\times r}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The surrogate is centred at z=H_n but the proof differentiates one centred at t=z vee delta. issues.failure_explanation: The displayed factor construction uses all other blocks at iteration n-1, creating simultaneous/Jacobi updates, while the invoked main BMM theorem uses newly updated blocks for indices below i. After correcting the separate dimensionally forced final-index typo in this line, Jacobi proximal ALS can have a nonstationary 2-cycle even on compact boxes. Explicitly, take f(u,v,w)=(18/5-uvw)^2 on [0,3]^3, rho=16/5 and initial point (1,1,1). Each exact simultaneous proximal block update at equal factors s gives s_new=(2(18/5)s^2+(16/5)s)/(2s^4+16/5). Thus (1,1,1) and (2,2,2) alternate forever; both points are interior and nonstationary.
issues.overall_effect: The printed ALS-PR branch of cor:NTF can violate both asymptotic stationarity and the decreasing stationarity bound, independent of MUR and compactness. The same stale-block pattern appears in the NMF MU/MUR displays.
